---
title: "WF1 — Build model"
---

`build_model.smk` builds a Wflow-SBM basin model from catalog data, runs it on historical forcing, and evaluates available observed variables. It supplies the model used by WF4.

## Rules

| Rule | Operation |
|---|---|
| `all` (target) | Collect model, simulation, figures, and records. |
| 1.01 `delineate_region` | Define the shared basin region. |
| 1.02 `delineate_subbasins_and_rivers` | Build shared vectors and location registry. |
| 1.03 `extract_climate_datasets` | Extract the selected historical climate source. |
| 1.04 `plot_climate_datasets` | Plot that source on its native grid. |
| 1.05 `prepare_land_and_soil_maps` | Prepare thematic rasters for model building. |
| 1.06 `build_wflow_model` | Build the Wflow-SBM model. |
| 1.07 `add_reservoirs_lakes_glaciers` | Add waterbodies and glaciers. |
| 1.08 `declare_gauges_and_outputs` | Configure gauges and Wflow output variables. |
| 1.09 `add_climate_forcing` | Add model forcing and complete the model. |
| 1.10 `write_gauge_index` | Map Wflow IDs to named stations. |
| 1.11 `plot_basin_map` | Plot basin and thematic maps. |
| 1.12 `plot_model_forcing` | Plot the model forcing grid. |
| 1.13 `run_historical_simulation` | Run Wflow on the historical window. |
| 1.14 `export_simulation_tables` | Export per-variable response tables. |
| 1.15 `plot_model_evaluation` | Plot and score against available observations. |
| 1.16 `write_run_metadata` | Record run identity and staleness metadata. |
| 1.17 `gather_benchmarks` | Merge benchmark parts. |
| 1.18 `gather_logs` | Merge log parts. |

The `all` target collects the products. The historical climate store feeds figures; model forcing is assembled from the configured data catalog in rule 1.09.

## Rule flow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["1.01–1.02 Region and vectors"] --> B["1.05–1.08 Build model and outputs"]
  A --> C["1.03–1.04 Historical climate"]
  B --> D["1.09 Add forcing"]
  C --> D
  D --> E["1.13 Historical simulation"]
  D --> F["1.10–1.12 Index and figures"]
  E --> G["1.14–1.16 Tables, evaluation, metadata"]
  F --> H["1.17–1.18 Records"]
  G --> H
```

The figure branches are terminal products; the historical simulation uses the completed model and forcing.

## Configuration

The project file, for example `test_case/project_config_rapid.yml`, supplies `project.catalog`, the `basin` definition and `output_locations`, `climate.selected` and `climate.window`, and `model.outvars`. Its `workflows.build_model` stanza enables this workflow and points to its YAML file through `config_path`.

The workflow file, `test_case/project_config_rapid_build_model.yml`, sets `engine.build_config` and `engine.waterbodies_config` to the hydromt recipes in `config/defaults/`, `simulation_window.start` and `.end` to the historical run years, and optional `observations` paths keyed by modeled variable. The template at `config/templates/project_config.build_model.template.yml` shows these keys; `engine` and `simulation_window` may be omitted to use the defaults. The run window must fit inside `climate.window`.

Wflow treats the run's start as the initial model state time. With daily forcing, the first update and output occur one day later: a run starting on January 1 requires forcing from January 2 through its end date. A store beginning on January 2 therefore covers that run; WF1 preserves the requested state time when HydroMT writes the forcing configuration. A later first stamp or an earlier final stamp still fails the coverage check.

```yaml
engine:
  build_config: config/defaults/wflow_build_model.yml
  waterbodies_config: config/defaults/wflow_update_waterbodies.yml
observations:
  river discharge: test_case/test_data/observations_timeseries.csv
simulation_window: {start: 2010, end: 2016}
```

## Inputs

Inputs include cataloged terrain, land, soil, hydrography, waterbody, and climate data; output locations; the two Wflow build recipes; and observations when evaluation is requested. The simulation window lies inside the historical climate window.

## Outputs

WF1 writes the basin vectors and thematic maps, the Wflow-SBM model and forcing, a gauge crosswalk, the native historical simulation response, exported per-variable tables, evaluation figures and metrics where observations are available, and run metadata. Logs and benchmarks are gathered at the project level. WF4 consumes the completed model, not the historical evaluation figures.
